headline: Rent growth holds, but rising costs squeeze net income
summary_short: NNN REIT reported FY2026 Q1 revenue of $240.4M, up 4.1% y/y and 0.8% q/q, while net income fell 2.6% y/y to $94.0M and diluted EPS was $0.50 versus $0.51 a year ago.
summary_long: Rental income grew 4.1% y/y to $240.4M on revenue from recent property acquisitions, while portfolio occupancy held at 98.6%. Net income fell 2.6% y/y to $94.0M as higher G&A (incentive compensation) and higher depreciation from the larger portfolio outweighed the revenue gain; interest expense also rose on a new $300M term loan drawn this quarter and a higher-rate, higher-average Credit Facility balance. NNN sold 25 properties (16 vacant, nine income-producing) for $36.3M in disposition proceeds and spent $142.3M on real estate additions. The board paid a $0.600/share dividend, up from $0.580 a year ago. No forward guidance was disclosed in the filing.

drivers.explanation: Revenue grew from recent property acquisitions, but higher incentive-compensation G&A, higher depreciation on the larger portfolio, and higher interest expense from a new $300M term loan draw outweighed the gain, pulling net income and EPS lower.
Rental income increased primarily due to revenue from NNN's recent property acquisitions.
Grew in line with revenue; non-reimbursed real estate expenses (net of tenant reimbursements) actually declined on fewer vacant properties.
G&A rose on higher incentive compensation and depreciation increased on the larger acquired portfolio, partially offset by recent dispositions.
Interest expense rose on a new $300M term loan drawn this quarter and a higher-average, higher-rate Credit Facility balance, compounding the G&A and depreciation increases.
Tracked the net income decline; weighted-average diluted shares outstanding rose modestly to 189.5M from 187.1M a year ago on continued at-the-market equity issuance.
